blocks.title: Why these schemes exist
blocks.markdown:
Small borrowers — a street vendor, a first-time entrepreneur, a marginal farmer — are creditworthy in substance but fail a bank's usual tests: no collateral, no credit history, tiny ticket size. Government schemes bridge that gap in one of three ways:

- **Guarantee** the loan, so the bank can lend without collateral and still be protected against default.
- **Subsidise** the loan, through a margin-money grant or an interest subvention, so the effective cost to the borrower falls.
- **Target** a borrower group and set simplified norms, so banks route a defined share of credit to it.

The loan is still made by a bank on its own books; the scheme changes the risk or the price, not the lender.

blocks.title: Credit-guarantee schemes
blocks.markdown:
A **credit-guarantee** scheme puts a fund between the bank and the loss. If a covered loan defaults, the fund pays the bank most of the shortfall, so the bank can lend collateral-free.

- **CGTMSE** — Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises. Set up by the Government and SIDBI, it guarantees collateral-free working-capital and term loans to micro and small enterprises up to a ceiling that has been raised several times. The bank pays an annual guarantee fee; the trust bears an agreed share of any default.
- Similar guarantee structures back parts of the education-loan and street-vendor schemes.

A guarantee is not a subsidy — the borrower still repays in full and at the normal rate; only the bank's downside is covered.

blocks.title: PMMY / MUDRA loan tiers
blocks.markdown:
The **Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)** covers collateral-free loans to non-farm micro-enterprises — manufacturing, trading, services — routed through banks, NBFCs and micro-finance institutions. **MUDRA** (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency, a SIDBI subsidiary) refinances the lenders and runs a guarantee.

Loans are grouped by size into named tiers:

- **Shishu** — the smallest loans, for a new or very small unit.
- **Kishore** — mid-sized loans for a unit that is growing.
- **Tarun** — the largest tier, for an established micro-enterprise scaling up.

Remember the *order and names* of the tiers; the rupee bands for each tier have been revised and a higher tier has since been added, so treat any specific figure as revisable.

blocks.title: Targeted-credit and subsidy schemes
blocks.markdown:
| Scheme | Who it targets | The facility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Stand-Up India** | At least one Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch | A bank loan for a *greenfield* (new) enterprise in manufacturing, services or trading |
| **PM SVANidhi** | Street vendors | A small collateral-free working-capital loan, stepped up on timely repayment, with an interest subsidy and a cashback for digital transactions |
| **KCC** — Kisan Credit Card | Farmers (also animal husbandry and fisheries) | A revolving short-term credit limit for crop and allied needs, with an interest subvention for prompt repayment |
| **PMEGP** — Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme | New micro-enterprises, often first-generation entrepreneurs | A bank loan with a **margin-money subsidy** (a grant that reduces the borrower's own contribution), administered with KVIC |
| **ECLGS** (historical) | Businesses hit by the COVID-19 disruption | A fully government-guaranteed emergency credit line, additional to existing limits — a time-bound scheme |

blocks.title: Common confusions
blocks.markdown:
- **A guarantee scheme and a subsidy scheme are different.** CGTMSE covers the bank's loss; PMEGP gives the borrower a margin-money grant; KCC and PM SVANidhi give an interest subsidy.
- **MUDRA is not a bank.** It is a refinance-and-guarantee agency; the loan is disbursed by a bank, NBFC or MFI.
- **Shishu / Kishore / Tarun are size tiers, not separate schemes**, all under PMMY.
- **Stand-Up India requires a *new* enterprise** and a borrower from the target group; it is not a general SC/ST loan.
- **KCC is a revolving limit, not a one-time loan**, and it now covers animal husbandry and fisheries, not only crops.
- **Treat every rupee ceiling as revisable.** The schemes' limits, subsidy rates and tenor are changed by notification; the exam-safe facts are the target group and the mechanism.

blocks.title: Quick revision
blocks.markdown:
- Schemes bridge the small-borrower gap by guaranteeing, subsidising or targeting a loan that a bank still makes on its own books.
- CGTMSE guarantees collateral-free loans to micro and small enterprises; the bank pays a fee and the trust bears a share of any default.
- PMMY / MUDRA: collateral-free loans to non-farm micro-enterprises in three named size tiers — Shishu, Kishore, Tarun (bands revised, a higher tier added). MUDRA refinances and guarantees; it is not a bank.
- Stand-Up India: a new enterprise loan for an SC/ST borrower and a woman borrower per branch. PM SVANidhi: stepped working-capital loans for street vendors with an interest subsidy. KCC: a revolving short-term limit for farmers with interest subvention. PMEGP: a bank loan with a margin-money subsidy for new micro-enterprises.
- Learn the target group and mechanism; treat rupee ceilings as revisable.

blocks.title: Practice
blocks.markdown:
One defensible answer each, with a one-line reason.

1. A scheme pays the bank most of its loss if a collateral-free micro-enterprise loan defaults. Guarantee or subsidy?
2. Under which scheme does a bank branch lend to at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower for a brand-new enterprise?
3. Shishu, Kishore and Tarun are tiers of which scheme?
4. A street vendor takes a first small working-capital loan and a larger one after repaying on time. Name the scheme.
5. A farmer needs a revolving limit for seeds and fertiliser, with cheaper interest if repaid promptly. Name the instrument.
6. PMEGP helps a new unit by giving the borrower a ____ , which reduces the borrower's own contribution.
7. True or false: MUDRA disburses loans directly to borrowers.
8. Why should you not memorise a specific rupee ceiling for these schemes as a hard fact?

**Answers:** 1 Guarantee — the borrower still repays in full; only the bank's downside is covered (CGTMSE-type). 2 Stand-Up India. 3 PMMY / MUDRA. 4 PM SVANidhi. 5 Kisan Credit Card (KCC). 6 margin-money subsidy (a grant). 7 False — MUDRA refinances and guarantees; a bank, NBFC or MFI disburses. 8 The ceilings, subsidy rates and tenor are revised by notification; only the target group and mechanism are stable.

flashcards.front: Three ways a government scheme helps a small borrower get bank credit?
flashcards.back: Guarantee the loan (bank protected against default), subsidise it (margin-money grant or interest subvention), or target a borrower group with simplified norms. The bank still makes the loan on its own books.
flashcards.explanation: The scheme changes the risk or the price, not the lender.

flashcards.back: It is a guarantee fund (Government + SIDBI) that lets banks give collateral-free loans to micro and small enterprises: the bank pays an annual fee, and the trust bears an agreed share of any default.
flashcards.explanation: A guarantee, not a subsidy — the borrower repays in full at the normal rate.

flashcards.front: Name the MUDRA / PMMY loan tiers in order of size.
flashcards.back: Shishu (smallest), Kishore (mid-sized), Tarun (largest). They are size bands under one scheme — PMMY — for collateral-free loans to non-farm micro-enterprises. The rupee bands have been revised.
flashcards.explanation: MUDRA refinances and guarantees the lenders; it is not a bank.

flashcards.front: Who does Stand-Up India target, and for what?
flashcards.back: At least one Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch, for a bank loan to set up a new (greenfield) enterprise in manufacturing, services or trading.
flashcards.explanation: It requires a new enterprise — not a general-purpose SC/ST loan.

flashcards.front: What is the Kisan Credit Card (KCC)?
flashcards.back: A revolving short-term credit limit for farmers (and now animal husbandry and fisheries) covering crop and allied needs, with an interest subvention for prompt repayment.
flashcards.explanation: A running limit, not a one-time loan.

flashcards.front: How does PMEGP help a borrower, versus PM SVANidhi?
flashcards.back: PMEGP gives a margin-money subsidy — a grant that reduces the borrower's own contribution to a new micro-enterprise loan. PM SVANidhi gives street vendors a stepped-up working-capital loan with an interest subsidy and a digital-transaction cashback.
flashcards.explanation: PMEGP subsidises capital cost; SVANidhi subsidises interest.

flashcards.front: Which facts about a government credit scheme are exam-safe, and which are not?
flashcards.back: Safe: the target group and the mechanism (guarantee / subsidy / targeting). Not safe: the exact rupee ceiling, subsidy rate and tenor — these are changed by notification.
flashcards.explanation: Learn the structure, not the current numbers.
